correctness.rationale: Necessity follows because two white open twins form an invariant stalled pair. For sufficiency, any nonempty white set with at most one vertex per twin class has a force: on a nonempty side choose a white vertex with maximal neighborhood and, if needed, the next-largest white neighborhood; strict nesting supplies a vertex adjacent to exactly the maximal white vertex. Induction then empties the white set. The product formula follows independently class by class. Exhaustive replay agrees on all 511 canonical connected chain-graph profiles through order 10 and all 349524 tested initial subsets.

broader_coverage.reasoning: DeAlba proves that unsaturated vertices of uniquely restricted matchings yield skew zero forcing sets and gives further minimum-set results under additional matching hypotheses. Cooper--Fickes gives broad closure/matroid theory. Neither inspected statement classifies every initial set of every chain graph, so no stronger theorem located implies the product formula.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification of every feasible initial set in a classical forcing process on the canonical nested-neighborhood bipartite class. It compresses the entire skew-zero-forcing set system to the open-twin partition, yields a factorized enumerator, and simultaneously determines the minimum number and number of minimum sets. This is structurally stronger than another isolated minimum-value calculation and can be used directly for enumeration, sampling, or reliability questions on chain graphs.
